Compare two Markov chains

Source: R/chainComparison.R
compareChains.Rd

Computes distances and divergences between two Markov chains on the same states and, when the chains are given as observed sequences, tests whether the sequences come from the same chain.

Usage

compareChains(
  x,
  y,
  base = exp(1),
  test = c("G", "Pearson", "simulation", "none"),
  ...
)

Arguments

x, y

Two markovchain objects with the same states (matched by name), or two observed sequences (character, factor or numeric vectors), from which the chains are estimated by maximum likelihood on the union of their states.

base

The base of the logarithm used by the divergences (default exp(1), nats).

test

For sequences, the test of equality of the two transition matrices passed to verifyHomogeneity: "G" (likelihood ratio, the default), "Pearson", "simulation" (Monte Carlo), or "none". Ignored for markovchain objects, whose sampling variability is not known.

...

Further arguments for verifyHomogeneity, such as B and seed.

Value

An object of class "markovchainComparison", a list with:

distances

A named vector: totalVariation, the largest row-wise total variation distance \(\max_i \frac12\sum_j |P_{ij} - Q_{ij}|\); weightedTotalVariation, the same row distances averaged with the stationary distribution of x; hellinger, the largest row-wise Hellinger distance \(\max_i \sqrt{\frac12 \sum_j (\sqrt{P_{ij}} - \sqrt{Q_{ij}})^2}\); frobenius, \(\|P - Q\|_F\); maximum, \(\max_{i,j}|P_{ij} - Q_{ij}|\); and stationary, the total variation distance between the two stationary distributions.

divergences

A named vector: rateXY and rateYX, the Kullback-Leibler divergence rates \(D(P\|Q)\) and \(D(Q\|P)\) (see divergenceRate); maxRowXY, the largest row-wise Kullback-Leibler divergence of \(P\) from \(Q\); and jensenShannon, the largest row-wise Jensen-Shannon divergence, which is symmetric and finite.

stationaryDistributions

A two-row matrix with the stationary distributions of x and y.

test

For sequences, the htest returned by verifyHomogeneity; otherwise NULL.

x, y

The two chains, as markovchain objects.

Details

The measures that depend on a stationary distribution (weightedTotalVariation, stationary, rateXY, rateYX) are NA when the chain concerned has more than one. The row-wise measures and their names follow PyDTMC's calculate_transition_distance, calculate_transition_divergence and calculate_stationary_distance, which give the same values.

For two sequences the test is that of Anderson and Goodman (1957) and Kullback, Kupperman and Ku (1962): the hypothesis that both come from the same chain, against different transition matrices. Each sequence is treated as one sample; for several sequences per group, or for counts, call verifyHomogeneity directly.

References

Anderson, T. W. and Goodman, L. A. (1957). Statistical inference about Markov chains. The Annals of Mathematical Statistics, 28(1), 89-110.

Kullback, S., Kupperman, M. and Ku, H. H. (1962). Tests for contingency tables and Markov chains. Technometrics, 4(4), 573-608.

Rached, Z., Alajaji, F. and Campbell, L. L. (2004). The Kullback-Leibler divergence rate between Markov sources. IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, 50(5), 917-921. doi:10.1109/TIT.2004.826687

See also

divergenceRate, verifyHomogeneity, autoplot.markovchain (type = "comparison")

Examples

s <- c("a", "b", "c")
P <- new("markovchain", states = s, transitionMatrix = matrix(
  c(0.5, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1, 0.6, 0.3, 0.25, 0.25, 0.5), 3, byrow = TRUE,
  dimnames = list(s, s)))
Q <- new("markovchain", states = s, transitionMatrix = matrix(
  c(0.4, 0.4, 0.2, 0.2, 0.5, 0.3, 0.3, 0.1, 0.6), 3, byrow = TRUE,
  dimnames = list(s, s)))
compareChains(P, Q)
#> Comparison of two Markov chains on 3 states
#> 
#> Distances:
#>         totalVariation weightedTotalVariation              hellinger 
#>                0.15000                0.11720                0.14250 
#>              frobenius                maximum             stationary 
#>                0.27390                0.15000                0.08825 
#> 
#> Divergences (rates weighted by the stationary distributions):
#>        rateXY        rateYX      maxRowXY jensenShannon 
#>       0.05428       0.05066       0.09233       0.02002 

# two sequences: distances between the estimated chains, and a test
set.seed(1)
x <- rmarkovchain(300, P, t0 = "a")
y <- rmarkovchain(300, Q, t0 = "a")
compareChains(x, y)
#> Comparison of two Markov chains on 3 states
#> 
#> Distances:
#>         totalVariation weightedTotalVariation              hellinger 
#>                0.22240                0.16940                0.16930 
#>              frobenius                maximum             stationary 
#>                0.38190                0.22240                0.04333 
#> 
#> Divergences (rates weighted by the stationary distributions):
#>        rateXY        rateYX      maxRowXY jensenShannon 
#>       0.09151       0.09950       0.10150       0.02804 
#> 
#> Test that both sequences come from the same chain:
#>   G-squared = 27.89, df = 6, p-value = 9.851e-05
